target_name: Hard Capital Stock Under Demand Uncertainty
rationale: A defensible stock-versus-flow reformulation of the archive's best joint result, though ppent/(ppent+R&D stock) collapses to little more than an inverse R&D-intensity rank, so the signal risks being the already-explored "uncertainty × low knowledge" pairing in new clothing rather than a genuine test of capital commitment.

Four archived acquisition-gate signals already delivered nearly identical -4.5% to -5.4% alphas with negligible Fama-MacBeth slopes, which is the fingerprint of a single acquirer-underperformance main effect (a well-known published anomaly) rather than an interaction, and the heavily zero-inflated three-year aqc share makes the ranks lumpy and the portfolio composition unstable, so this is likely a fifth draw from the same well.

The stated justification is factually wrong — xrd/(capx+xrd) is a strictly decreasing transform of the parent's capx/(capx+xrd), so its rank is an exact reversal and the only incremental content in the product is the additive uncertainty main effect RANK(VOL), making this a near-mechanical relabelling that cannot decompose the parent's long and short legs as claimed.

A clean single-variable substitution on a validated mechanism with a better-scaled, zero-mass-free conditioning leg, but the external-financing leg is essentially the published net-external-financing anomaly and the hard/soft mix leg is heavily correlated with the R&D-intensity gate it replaces, so the expected incremental information is modest.

The expected negative sign fights the well-documented positive main effect of R&D intensity, and in an unsigned rank-product that main effect will dominate the spread, so the design cannot separate option-conversion from the R&D anomaly; it is also close to the mirror image of the archived "Plant Contraction With Research Intensification," and "informative regardless of sign" is an admission that the hypothesis is not sharply specified.

The best-diagnosed proposal here — it correctly identifies the distressed-shrinking-firm tilt as the source of the parent's sign conflict between slope and alpha, and substitutes a conditioning leg with demonstrated long-side alpha while introducing a genuinely new labor-productivity dimension, though it remains cousin to the archive's gross-profit-scaling family and should be checked for overlap with the profitability factor.
